clue.text: Rendering of inferno after hot tin? Huge pity!

definitions.text: Rendering of inferno after hot tin? Huge pity!

indicators.note: a rendering is a new version of something, so the following words are reworked into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone laments a hellish blaze that followed something hot in a tin can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rendering' is the anagram signal for all the remaining words. The whole clue also works as the definition: going from a hot tin to an inferno is moving from one bad situation to a worse one.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb describes escaping one trouble only to land in a worse one, as the clue's hot tin giving way to an inferno does.

clue.text: UK charters?

parts.note: charters read as people who make charts, so the clue asks for Britain's national map-making agency rather than documents granting rights

explanation.definitionFit: The national mapping agency of Great Britain draws the country's official maps, so it is the UK's chart-maker.

clue.text: This evening drink is drawing near

indicators.note: drawing here means pulling in, so the word for a drink takes another word inside it

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits
nigh is an old word for near

explanation.surface: Tonight someone's drink is getting closer.
explanation.definitionFit: A direct synonym: the adverb names this coming evening, the same as the clue's phrase.

clue.text: Row after resistance in charge is not from the battery

indicators.note: after puts the row word behind the rest
in places the resistance symbol within the word for a charge

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
a range is a row, as of mountains

explanation.surface: Something in a row behind a resistor is not powered by the battery, an electrical picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The electrical surface (resistance, charge, battery) hides the farming sense: battery here means battery farming, where hens are caged.
explanation.definitionFit: Free-range poultry and eggs come from birds allowed outdoors, the opposite of battery-farmed hens kept in cages.

clue.text: This spirit would be the greatest proof of all

definitions.text: This spirit would be the greatest proof of all

parts.words: This spirit would be the greatest proof of all
parts.note: proof is the measure of alcohol strength, and a spirit that was pure alcohol would hit the maximum on the scale; the phrase also means total commitment

explanation.definitionFit: Pure alcohol would be entirely alcohol, a full measure, and the phrase is also an idiom for wholehearted effort.

clue.text: Under pressure from being 1across 25

definitions.meaning: going from the pan straight into the flames means literally being exposed to warmth

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being stressed under pressure, and literally describes someone who has jumped from a frying pan into a fire.

clue.text: Plant with lofted precision when not using driving club

indicators.note: in a down clue, lofting a ball sends it up, so the remaining letters are read from bottom to top
not using means these letters are left out of the longer word

parts.note: accuracy is precision
the RAC (Royal Automobile Club) is a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: A golfer plays a lofted shot accurately without reaching for the driver.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf surface makes 'driving club' look like a driver. Removing RAC from ACCURACY leaves ACCUY, which 'lofted' turns upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The yucca is a spiky-leaved plant of the agave family, grown in gardens and as a houseplant.

clue.text: Only poor environment for women in city

indicators.note: an environment surrounds something, so the phrase for 'only poor' wraps around the women letter

parts.note: if there are only poor people, there are no rich

explanation.surface: Somewhere in the city only the poor surround the women.
explanation.definitionFit: Norwich is a cathedral city in Norfolk, in the east of England.

clue.text: 'tisn't negligent smashing natural hazard

indicators.note: smashing breaks the letters apart so they can be put back together differently

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a crashing accident wasn't due to carelessness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashing' looks like praise but signals the anagram of all fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This common weed stings anyone who brushes against it, a hazard found growing in nature.

clue.text: Waste to get long spell in prison

parts.note: dung is animal waste
an eon is a very long period of time

explanation.surface: Getting rid of waste earns a long stretch in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is a dark underground cell for prisoners, as in a castle.

clue.text: Clip king in bar

indicators.note: in places the king's letter inside the word for bar

parts.note: bar as a preposition means except, as in 'all bar one'
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king is cuffed while drinking in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub or a rod but is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: A clip is a short extract from a film, the same thing as an excerpt.

clue.text: Heard to predict when it's a bore

indicators.note: heard means the word is listened to, so it is spelt differently from how it sounds

parts.note: to augur is to foretell

explanation.surface: Someone is overheard forecasting when something will be tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bore' suggests a tedious person; here it is a tool that bores holes.
explanation.definitionFit: An auger is a tool for boring holes in wood or the ground, so it is literally something that bores.

clue.text: Collapse of sport with one race

parts.note: RU stands for Rugby Union
I is the Roman numeral for one
a race of people can be a nation

explanation.surface: A sport's decline is blamed on one particular race.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruination is the state of being ruined, a downfall or collapse.

clue.text: Like this fighting all the time?

definitions.text: Like this fighting all the time?

parts.words: Like this fighting all the time?
parts.note: two pets that are famous enemies are imagined scrapping endlessly, describing a bitter, constant quarrel

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a relationship of constant bickering, like the proverbial enmity of two household pets.

clue.text: I'd meat rejected by holy leader

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so both pieces together are read in reverse

parts.note: ham is a meat

explanation.surface: A religious leader turns down an offer of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns IDHAM backwards as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islam the Mahdi is a prophesied redeemer and spiritual leader expected to appear before the end of time.

clue.text: Spirits glow in the dark

definitions.meaning: illicitly distilled liquor, the bootlegger's sense
the light from the moon at night

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is illegally distilled liquor, the other the moon's light shining at night.

clue.text: Swell when poisonous weed lacks power

indicators.note: lacks means one letter is taken away from the weed's name

parts.note: spurge is a weed with a poisonous milky sap

explanation.surface: Something swells up when a toxic weed is weakened.
explanation.definitionFit: A surge is a swell, as in a sudden rise of the sea.

clue.text: Creamy cheese used in apricot tart

indicators.note: used in means the cheese is contained within the following words

explanation.surface: A creamy soft cheese goes into an apricot tart.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft, creamy Italian whey cheese often used in desserts.

clue.text: Drunken pool night exploring the nether regions

indicators.note: drunken suggests staggering about, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A drunken night by the pool ends with someone exploring underground.
explanation.definitionFit: Potholing is the British word for caving, exploring underground caves and shafts.

clue.text: See 4
See 5
El Al is name dissociated from unstable airlines

definitions.note: the clue names an airline; the answer is the adjective for its nationality

indicators.note: unstable means shaky, so the remaining letters are shuffled
dissociated from means separated off, so this letter is taken out

explanation.surface: El Al is said to stand apart from shaky airlines.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing N from AIRLINES leaves AIRLIES, which 'unstable' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: El Al is the national flag carrier of Israel, so it is an Israeli airline.

clue.text: Of course Nijinsky was one

parts.note: Nijinsky suggests the ballet dancer, but it was also the name of a famous winner on the turf; 'of course' hints at a racecourse

explanation.definitionFit: Nijinsky was a champion thoroughbred that won the English Triple Crown in 1970, named after the dancer.

clue.text: Island's greeting around part of Hispaniola

indicators.note: around puts the greeting on either side of the island word

parts.note: hi is a greeting
an ait is a small river island, as on the Thames

explanation.surface: An islander's greeting circles part of a Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti occupies the western third of the Caribbean island of Hispaniola, which it shares with the Dominican Republic.

clue.text: South American Indian tribe found in the foothills?

parts.note: the Cree are a First Nations people of Canada

explanation.surface: A South American tribe is discovered living in the foothills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' reads as one phrase but splits into S and an American Indian tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: Scree is loose broken rock that collects on slopes at the base of mountains.

clue.text: Weave in between, but not be woven

indicators.note: woven means twisted together, so these letters are interlaced into a new order
but not means these letters are excluded from the word before

explanation.surface: Someone is told to weave in between threads but not be woven themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface seems to say the answer must not itself be woven, but 'woven' is the anagram signal applied to INTWEEN, left once 'but not' drops the two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To entwine is to twist or weave things together.

clue.text: Demanding information that's going around

indicators.note: around means the departure word surrounds the information word

parts.note: an exit is a going out, a departure
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone demands the news that is circulating.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent means pressing or demanding, as in exigent circumstances.
